note: Each case recreates a rule 7 or rule 11.5 situation on the hand-written fixture board. The citation names the rule and gives the situation in the project's words. The hex names are fixture hexes, not board 1 hexes.

cases.citation: Units may always fire into an adjacent hex regardless of terrain.
Adjacent hexes are in LOS even when the target is a woods hex.
Units in the same building may not see each other when the LOS crosses a building symbol in an intervening hex. The rulebook example is N3 to N5.
Units in the same building see each other when the LOS crosses no building symbol in an intervening hex. The rulebook example is N3 to M5.
A unit in a multi-story building fires over a building of 2 hexes or smaller. The rulebook example is T2 over T4 to T6.
The hex directly behind the obstacle is a blind hex. The rulebook example is T5 behind T4.
The unit may fire at the obstacle hex itself. The rulebook example is T4.
The unit may fire at the hex before the obstacle. The rulebook example is T3.
Units on ground level see over intervening obstacles to multi-story buildings.
Fire from ground level at a multi-story building cannot come from a blind hex.
LOS extends into a woods or building symbol but not through it.
The same LOS from the other end.
A woods symbol in an intervening hex stops the LOS.
Multi-story buildings obstruct all LOS regardless of elevation, here between two multi-story buildings.
Symbols in the firing or target hex do not obstruct the LOS.
A LOS may not be traced through a wall hexside unless it ends or originates in the hex that hexside forms.
The LOS originates in the hex that the wall hexside forms.
The LOS ends in the hex that the wall hexside forms.
A LOS traced exactly along a hexside passes through one of the adjoining hexes at the firer's choice. Here H4 is woods and H5 is open.
The hexes crossed by a LOS are in firer-to-target order for penetration. A hex beside the LOS is not on it.
Wheat hexes on the LOS are counted as hindrances. The modifier waits for rule 44.
